> A compact desktop robot that translates software debugging data into physical expressions. Connected via USB-C, a background PC companion script uses Python's traceback module to catch code failures (like NameErrors or SyntaxErrors) and transmits the data over serial to an ESP32-S3. BUGBOT then uses an expressive top display for digital facial animations, a dedicated chest screen for error readouts, and integrated RGB LEDs/buzzers to guide me through fixing my code

Spent this session expanding the core hardware architecture for BUGBOT within the KiCad Schematic Editor grid environment. Transitioned from baseline repository staging to active localized module footprint placement. Focused heavily on configuring our primary feedback peripherals, successfully sourcing and stamping down our WS2812B addressable RGB expression light module onto the white background drawing canvas. Evaluated the electrical pin layout arrays—including VDD, VSS ground rails, and the primary DIN/DOUT serial data cascade lines. This configuration successfully concludes our initial logic layout phase, establishing the bulletproof visual-first foundation needed ahead of next week's display screen data bus trace wire routings
